## What privacy mode records

| Still recorded | Never collected |
|----------------|-----------------|
| Number of clicks | IP address |
| The hour each click happened | Country, region, city and postcode |
| Browser and device type (for example Safari, iOS) | Internet provider and network |
| Whether the click was a bot | Referring website |
| Which destination the click went to | URL parameters (including ad click IDs) |
| | Full user-agent string and device fingerprint |

Click times are kept to the **hour**, not the second. An exact timestamp can sometimes be matched against the destination website's own logs to pick out an individual visit, so we don't keep one.

Your visitor's IP address still has to reach our servers to deliver the redirect, as with any website. For a privacy-mode link it is used only for that, and for bot filtering at the moment of the click, then discarded. It is not stored in your click data, our analytics database or our application logs.

**Video: GDPR Compliant URL Shortener: Track Clicks Without Personal Data** — https://www.youtube.com/embed/A42od01ogZQ

Some links shouldn't track the people who click them: a QR code on a patient leaflet, a link in a letter from the council, a campaign where you've promised not to profile anyone. Linkly's privacy mode counts the clicks on a link or QR code without keeping anything that identifies the visitor.

- 0:00 — Links that shouldn't track people
- 0:12 — What a click normally records
- 0:36 — Turn on privacy mode
- 0:47 — What switches off
- 1:03 — What still works
- 1:16 — The click report
- 1:26 — The catch: no unique visitors

## How to turn on privacy mode for a link

1. **Open the link you want to make private, or click **Create New Link**.** — Privacy mode works on any link, including links you have already printed as QR codes. Turning it on doesn't change the short link or the QR code.

2. **Under **Tracking & analytics**, open **Privacy mode**.** — It's in the list of tracking settings, just after **Conversion tracking**.

3. **Turn on **Record clicks anonymously**.** — The section shows exactly what is still recorded and what is never collected, and an **On** badge appears next to its title.

4. **Click **Save**.** — From this point on, every click on the link is recorded anonymously. The link page shows a **Privacy mode** badge next to the link's name, so you can see at a glance which links are private.

## Settings privacy mode switches off

Some link settings exist to collect or pass on information about the visitor, so they can't be combined with privacy mode. Turning privacy mode on switches them off for that link:

* **[Tracking pixels](https://linklyhq.com/support/retargeting-tracking-pixels)** (Meta, Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, TikTok, LinkedIn and the rest)
* **Custom tracking scripts**

They stay visible in the link editor, greyed out and marked **Off in privacy mode**, so it's always clear what the setting is doing:

![Tracking pixels, custom tracking scripts and conversion tracking greyed out and marked "Off in privacy mode"](https://linklyhq.com/img/privacy-mode-locked-settings.png)

![Webhooks and click notifications greyed out and marked "Off in privacy mode"](https://linklyhq.com/img/privacy-mode-automation-locked.png)

Webhooks deserve a special mention. A webhook arrives the moment someone clicks, so even an empty one would reveal the exact second of the visit. Privacy-mode links therefore send **no click webhooks at all**, including to webhooks set up for your whole workspace, and they don't appear in the live click feed.

If you turn privacy mode off later, these settings stay off. Nothing is switched back on without you choosing to.

## What still works

Everything that decides where a visitor goes, rather than records who they are:

* **Editing the destination.** Change the link or QR code's target whenever you like.

## Analytics for a privacy-mode link

Click totals, the daily (and hourly) chart, browser and device-type reports, and bot filtering all work as normal. Reports that rely on personal data stay empty: location, internet provider, referrer, URL parameters and unique visitors. The analytics page explains why, so an empty report doesn't look like missing data:

![The analytics page notice: "Privacy mode is on: clicks are counted without location, internet provider, referrer or URL parameters, so those reports stay empty."](https://linklyhq.com/img/privacy-mode-analytics-notice.png)

## Privacy mode and GDPR

Privacy mode is designed for links where collecting personal data is a problem: patient-facing material, where even knowing that someone scanned a QR code on a medicine leaflet can count as health data; public-sector communications; or any campaign where you have committed not to profile the audience.

Because a privacy-mode link stores no IP address, location, identifier or exact timestamp, its click records contain no personal data about the visitor. That makes it much simpler to describe in a data protection impact assessment or a medical-legal review. You should still check how your own organisation's requirements apply. Our [GDPR page](https://linklyhq.com/support/gdpr) covers how Linkly handles data for ordinary links.

### Can I still change where the link goes?

Yes. Privacy mode only changes what is recorded about each click. You can edit the destination as often as you like.

### Are clicks still counted?

Yes. Every click is counted, with its hour, browser and device type, and whether it came from a bot. Privacy-mode clicks count towards your plan's click allowance like any other click.

### Can I still redirect by country?

Yes. The visitor's country is worked out at the moment of the click to pick the right destination, then discarded. It is never stored.

### Can I turn privacy mode on through the API?

Yes. Set `privacy_mode` to `true` when creating or updating a link with the [API](https://linklyhq.com/url-shortener-api-reference). Turning it on clears the link's pixels, custom scripts, conversion tracking, webhooks and click notifications, just as it does in the app.

### Which plans include privacy mode?

All paid plans. If your workspace moves to the free plan, links that already use privacy mode stay private, and you can still turn it off.

**Available on:** Starter, Pro, Business, Enterprise plans

# Stripe Integration - Track Which Links Make Sales

> Connect Stripe to Linkly and see which short links produce revenue. Payments, subscription renewals and refunds are recorded against the link that was clicked.

Source: https://linklyhq.com/support/stripe-integration

# Linkly & Stripe

Click counts tell you a link was popular. They don't tell you it made any money.

Install the [Linkly app from the Stripe App Marketplace](https://marketplace.stripe.com/apps/linkly-conversion-tracking) and every payment that came through a tracked Linkly link is recorded against that link. You can then compare emails, ads, creators and campaigns by revenue, not only by clicks. Subscription renewals are credited to the link that first won the customer, and refunds are subtracted.

## What you need

- A Linkly account. The free plan works.
- A Stripe account. The app is free, and it only reads: it never creates charges or changes anything in Stripe.

## Install and connect

1. Install **[Linkly Conversion Tracking](https://marketplace.stripe.com/apps/linkly-conversion-tracking)** from the Stripe App Marketplace. After installing you land on the app's settings page.
2. Click **Connect to Linkly**. A new tab opens on Linkly.
3. Sign in to Linkly, choose the workspace this Stripe account belongs to, and click **Connect Stripe**.
4. Back in Stripe, click **Check again**. The page shows the workspace you connected.

Until a workspace is connected, nothing is recorded.

![The app's settings page in Stripe after connecting: "Connected to Demo Workspace", with the finish-setting-up notes below](https://linklyhq.com/img/stripe-app-connected.png)

## Track Stripe Payment Links (no code)

1. In Linkly, create a link that points at your Stripe Payment Link, for example `https://buy.stripe.com/abc123`, or edit one you already have.
2. In the link's **Tracking & analytics** options, switch on **Conversion tracking**.

That is the whole setup. Share the short link as usual. When someone clicks it, Linkly adds a short random identifier for that click to the Payment Link address as `client_reference_id`. Stripe hands it back when the payment completes, and Linkly matches the payment to the click.

If your Payment Link already uses `client_reference_id` for your own reconciliation, Linkly leaves your value alone and that link's payments can't be matched. Use the metadata method below instead.

## Track your own checkout

If you create Checkout Sessions in your own code, pass the click identifier yourself. Add the Linkly script to your site:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.linklyhq.com/linkly.js" async></script>
```

Read the identifier in the browser with `linkly('id')`, send it to your server with the order, and set it when you create the session:

```js
const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({
  client_reference_id: linklyClickId,
  // ...the rest of your session
});
```

If `client_reference_id` is already taken, put it in the metadata instead, as `linkly_cid`, on the Checkout Session or on the Customer:

```js
await stripe.customers.create({
  email: user.email,
  metadata: { linkly_cid: linklyClickId },
});
```

A customer created with a click identifier is recorded as a lead, and every payment that customer makes afterwards is credited to the same link.

## What gets recorded

| Stripe event | What Linkly records |
|--------------|---------------------|
| **Checkout completed** | A sale with the amount, tax and currency. A free trial is recorded as a lead. |
| **Invoice paid** | A sale for the first invoice, a renewal for the ones that follow. |
| **Charge refunded** | A negative sale against the same link, so revenue nets out. |
| **Customer created or updated** | A lead, when the customer carries a click identifier. |

A few things worth knowing:

- **Only tracked links count.** Payments that didn't come through a Linkly link with conversion tracking on are ignored. Linkly never sees the rest of your sales.
- **A subscription counts once per payment.** Stripe reports the first payment of a subscription twice, as a checkout and as an invoice. Linkly records it once.
- **Delayed payment methods.** For bank debits and vouchers, the sale is recorded when the money arrives, not when the checkout is completed.
- **Test mode works.** Payments made in Stripe test mode or a sandbox are recorded too, which is the easiest way to check your setup. They are marked as test payments.
- **The identifier names a click, not a person.** It is random and carries no personal information.

## In the Stripe Dashboard

Open any payment in Stripe and the Linkly panel shows which short link it came from, how it was matched, the amount recorded, and a link to that link's analytics in Linkly. For a renewal it shows the link that first brought the customer in.

![A payment in the Stripe Dashboard with the Linkly panel open: the link "Autumn sale", how it was matched, and £49.00 recorded in Linkly](https://linklyhq.com/img/stripe-app-payment-panel.png)

When a payment is refunded, in full or in part, the panel shows the refund and what the link is still credited with.

![The same payment after a £19.00 partial refund: the panel reads "Refunded: £19.00, so this link is credited with £30.00"](https://linklyhq.com/img/stripe-app-refund-panel.png)

## Disconnect

Open the app's settings in Stripe and click **Disconnect**, or uninstall the app. Either one stops recording immediately. Conversions already recorded stay in your reports.

## Troubleshooting

**Payments aren't appearing.** Check that conversion tracking is on for the link, then click the short link yourself and confirm the Stripe address contains `client_reference_id=linkly_`. If it shows your own value instead, use the metadata method.

**The panel says "Connect your Linkly workspace".** The app is installed but no workspace is connected yet. Open the app's settings in Stripe (Apps, then Installed apps, then Linkly Conversion Tracking) and click **Connect to Linkly**.

**Links to a hosted invoice.** A link that points at an `invoice.stripe.com` page can't carry a click identifier, so those payments aren't matched yet.

# How to Make a QR Code for a Google Form

A Google Form link is around ninety characters of letters and numbers. It works fine in an email, but nobody standing in front of a noticeboard, a sign-up sheet or a slide is going to type it into their phone. A **QR code** does the same job in one scan: point the camera, the form opens, they fill it in.

Google Forms does not have a QR code button of its own, so you need something to turn the form's link into a QR code. This guide uses Linkly, which gives you a QR code that you can **edit after printing** and that **counts every scan**, for free.

## Static or dynamic?

A free QR generator encodes the form's address directly into the QR code. That is a *static* QR code, and it is frozen: when next term's sign-up uses a new form, every printed copy still opens the old one.

Linkly makes *dynamic* QR codes. The QR code points at a short link, and the short link points at the form. Change the link's destination and every QR code already printed follows it, and because each scan passes through the link you can see how many people scanned, when, and where. The [static vs dynamic QR codes](https://linklyhq.com/blog/static-vs-dynamic-qr-codes) guide explains the difference in more detail.

**Video: How to Make a QR Code for a Google Form (Free)** — https://www.youtube.com/embed/fPmKC-VMnQA

Want a QR code for a Google Form? Here's how to make one in Linkly: copy the responder link, paste it in, and print the QR code on a sign. Nobody has to type a ninety character URL, and when next term's form is a new one you point the same QR code at it instead of reprinting.

- 0:00 — Why nobody types the link
- 0:22 — Get the form link, make the QR code
- 0:56 — Swap the form, keep the sign
- 1:09 — Every scan is counted

## See how many people scanned

Every scan is a click on the short link, so Linkly's [QR code analytics](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-analytics) show you how many people scanned the QR code, when, from which town, and on what kind of phone. That tells you whether the sign is in the right spot, whether the noticeboard gets read at all, and which of several signs is pulling its weight.

If you have the same form in several places, make one short link per place, each with its own QR code. They all open the same form, but you get a scan count for each.

## Tips for Google Form QR codes

* **Put a short instruction next to the QR code**, such as "Scan to sign up" or "Scan to give feedback". People scan when they know what they will get.
* **Check who can respond.** In the form's **Settings**, under **Responses**, an option restricts the form to people in your organisation. Leave it off for a public sign-up, or scanners with personal Google accounts will be asked to sign in and turned away.
* **Pre-filled links work too.** Google Forms can produce a link with some answers already filled in (**⋮ → Get pre-filled link**). Put one behind each QR code and you can tell which sign, table or event a response came from, even before you look at the scan counts.
* **Keep it big enough.** A QR code printed smaller than about 2 cm across is hard to scan from arm's length. Leave a clear margin around it.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I see who scanned the QR code?

You can see how many people scanned it, when, from roughly where, and on what device. You cannot see who they were unless the form itself asks for their name or email.

## Related QR code guides

- **[Create QR Codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/create-qr-codes)** - the complete guide to dynamic QR codes in Linkly

**Available on:** Free, Starter, Pro, Business, Enterprise plans

## How to create a Google review QR code

1. **Get your Google review link.** — Sign in to Google as your business and open your **Business Profile** (search for your business name in Google, or open Google Maps). Click **Ask for reviews** and copy the link. It opens your business's review box directly.

2. **Sign in to Linkly and click **Create New Link**.** — [Create a free account](https://l.linklyhq.com/l/4a) if you don't have one yet. The free plan covers a small shop easily.

3. **Paste the review link into the **Destination** field.** — Give the link a short ending such as `/review`, and a **Nickname** such as "Reviews - table cards" so you can tell your QR codes apart later.

4. **Click **Save**.** — Same destination, same star box, but now it is a link you own. The QR code is drawn as soon as the link exists.

5. **Download the QR code and send it to print.** — Click the QR code to add your colours or logo, then download a **PNG** or an **SVG** for whoever prints your table cards. See [adding a logo to a QR code](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-logo).

6. **Scan it yourself first.** — Point a phone at the QR code on your screen. It should land on your business's review box with the stars ready to tap.

## What customers see

The scan opens your business's Google review box, with the star rating ready to tap and a box for the comment. If the Google Maps app is installed it opens there; otherwise it opens in the browser. Customers who are not signed in to Google are asked to sign in first, which is Google's rule, not something the QR code controls.

You cannot pre-select the rating. The QR code opens the box, and people write what they write.

## Where to put it

* **Table cards and tent cards**, which is usually the winner for cafés and restaurants.
* **The counter or the till**, at the moment people are paying and pleased.
* **Receipts and invoices**, printed or emailed.
* **Packaging inserts** for online orders, with a line thanking them for the purchase.
* **After-service messages** by SMS or email, where the same short link works as a tappable link.
* **Your email signature**, for a service business.

Whatever you print, put a short line next to the QR code: "Enjoyed your visit? Scan to leave us a Google review." People scan when they know what will happen.

## Which spot actually works

Here is the trick worth stealing from the video. Make **one QR code per placement**: one short link for the table cards, another for the till receipts, another for the packaging insert. They all open the same review box, but each has its own scan count in [Linkly's analytics](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-analytics), so a month later you can see which spot brings the reviews in and print more of that one.

If you run more than one location, make one link per location too, each pointing at that location's review link.

## Changing where the QR code goes

Because the QR code points at a short link, its destination can change later. Open a new branch and repoint the old cards. Decide you would rather collect Tripadvisor or Trustpilot reviews for a while, and switch the same QR code over. If a review link ever changes, edit the link once and every card in the building follows.

## A note on Google's rules

Google's review policies allow you to ask customers for reviews, and a QR code is a good way to do it. They do not allow offering discounts or gifts in exchange for reviews, or showing the review link only to customers you expect to be positive. Ask everyone, and let the reviews speak for themselves.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where do I find my Google review link?

Sign in to Google as your business, open your Business Profile and click **Ask for reviews**. The link it shows opens your review box directly. Paste it into Linkly as the destination.

### Can the QR code pre-select five stars?

No. The scan opens the review box with the stars empty. Customers choose the rating themselves.

### Do customers need the Google Maps app?

No. If the app is installed the review box opens there, otherwise it opens in the browser. Customers do need to be signed in to a Google account to post a review, which is Google's requirement.

### Can I see how many people scanned it?

Yes. Every scan is a click on the short link, so you see totals over time, by placement if you made one link per placement, and by device. Google shows you the reviews themselves.

### Is it free?

Yes. Every Linkly link comes with a QR code, including on the [free plan](https://linklyhq.com/support/free-plan), and the QR codes do not expire.

## Related QR code guides

- **[Create QR Codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/create-qr-codes)** - the complete guide to dynamic QR codes in Linkly

**Available on:** Free, Starter, Pro, Business, Enterprise plans

# How to Make a QR Code for a Location

An address printed on a flyer, a poster or an invitation means someone has to read it, type it into a maps app, and get it right. A **location QR code** skips all of that: one scan and Google Maps opens on the pin, with the directions button already there.

Any maps link works. This guide uses Google Maps because it is on almost every phone, but a link from Apple Maps, Waze or any other map service can go behind the QR code in exactly the same way.

## Why make it with Linkly?

A free QR generator bakes the map link into the QR code itself, so the QR code is frozen from the moment it is printed. Linkly's QR codes point at a short link instead, which means:

* **You can move the pin later.** If the venue changes, edit the link and every printed QR code sends people to the new place.
* **Every scan is counted**, with the city it was scanned in and the kind of phone that scanned it.
* **The QR code can carry your logo and colours**, and live on your own domain.

**Video: Location QR Code Generator: One Scan Opens Google Maps** — https://www.youtube.com/embed/dEeKjoiXUfk

Want a QR code that opens your location in Google Maps? Here's how to make one in Linkly: copy the place link out of Maps, paste it in, and print the QR code. Nobody types an address, and if the venue changes you point the same QR code somewhere else.

- 0:00 — Getting people to the door
- 0:23 — Copy the link out of Maps, make the QR code
- 0:50 — What the scan opens
- 1:00 — When the venue moves
- 1:16 — Every scan is counted

## How to create a location QR code

1. **Copy the place link out of Google Maps.** — Find the place in Google Maps, click or tap **Share**, and choose **Copy link**. The link opens the pin with the directions button ready. If you want the QR code to open turn-by-turn directions straight away, get directions to the place first and share from there instead.

2. **Sign in to Linkly and click **Create New Link**.** — [Create a free account](https://l.linklyhq.com/l/4a) if you don't have one yet.

3. **Paste the map link into the **Destination** field.** — Give the link a short ending you can say out loud, such as `/venue` or `/find-us`, and a **Nickname** such as "Summer fair venue" so you can find it again in a month.

4. **Click **Save**.** — The short link and its QR code come back together. There is no separate generator step.

5. **Download the QR code.** — Click the QR code to style it and download a **PNG** for print or an **SVG** if a designer is laying out the flyer. See [SVG QR codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-svg) for the print workflow.

6. **Scan it before you print.** — Point a phone at the QR code on your screen. Google Maps should open on the pin, in the app if it is installed and in the browser if not.

## What the scan opens

On a phone with the Google Maps app installed, the QR code opens the app on your pin, with **Directions** one tap away. Without the app, it opens the same place in the browser. Either way the person gets there without typing anything.

If most of your visitors use iPhones and you would rather open Apple Maps, share the place from Apple Maps instead and paste that link. A Waze link works the same way for drivers.

## When the venue moves

Venues move, rooms change, and the flyers are usually already printed when it happens. Open the link in Linkly, paste the new place's link into **Destination**, and save. The short link and the printed QR code stay exactly as they were; everyone who scans from then on is sent to the right place.

The same edit turns a one-off QR code into a permanent one. A "find us" QR code on your business card can follow you to a new office, and the QR code on a market stall's sign can point at this week's pitch.

## Every scan is counted

Because the QR code runs through a short link, Linkly's [analytics](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-analytics) show how many people scanned it, when, which cities they were in, and what kind of phone they used. If you print the same location on flyers for three neighbourhoods, give each batch its own short link and QR code, and you will know where the next stack of flyers should go.

## Where location QR codes get used

* **Event flyers and posters**, so the address at the bottom becomes one scan.
* **Business cards and email signatures** for a shop or clinic.
* **Menus and table cards** that point at your second location.
* **Property boards and parcel labels**, where the address is the whole point.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I see how many people scanned it?

Yes. Every scan is a click on the short link, so you see totals over time, the cities people scanned from, and their device type.

### Is it free?

Yes. Every Linkly link comes with a QR code, including on the [free plan](https://linklyhq.com/support/free-plan), and the QR codes do not expire.

### Can I add my logo to the QR code?

Yes. Click the QR code in Linkly to change its colours and add a logo. See [adding a logo to a QR code](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-logo).

## Related QR code guides

- **[Create QR Codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/create-qr-codes)** - the complete guide to dynamic QR codes in Linkly

**Available on:** Free, Starter, Pro, Business, Enterprise plans

# Power Automate Integration - Create Short Links and Pull Click Data From Your Flows

> Use the certified Linkly connector in Microsoft Power Automate to create short links, read click analytics and record conversions from any flow. Sign in with Linkly, no API key needed.

Source: https://linklyhq.com/support/power-automate-integration

# Linkly & Power Automate

## What is Power Automate?

**Microsoft Power Automate** is Microsoft's automation platform. A flow starts from a trigger, such as a new row in Excel, an item added to a SharePoint list, a form submitted or a schedule, and then runs a series of actions across Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Dataverse and hundreds of other services.

With the Linkly connector, one of those actions can be **Create or update a link**, and another can be **Get click analytics**. Short links get created where your data already lives, and click data flows back into the tools your team already reads.

## How to use Linkly & Power Automate

Linkly publishes a **certified connector** for the Power Platform. It is built and maintained by Linkly, signed in with your Linkly account, and needs no API key.

With the connector, a flow can:

* **Create short links** with a custom domain, slug, UTM parameters, retargeting pixels and social preview, then write the short URL back to the row, record or message that triggered it.
* **Update or trash existing links** by ID, for example to change a destination when a campaign page moves.
* **Read click analytics**: clicks over time for a workspace or a set of links, filtered by date, country, browser, platform, referrer or ISP.
* **Get click counts by dimension** such as country, city, platform, referrer or UTM parameter.
* **Record conversions** against the link that was clicked, and list recent conversions.

The connector is certified, which means Microsoft has reviewed and published it and it appears in the connector picker like any Microsoft connector. Certified connectors from third parties are classed as **Premium** in Power Automate, so your Microsoft licence needs to include premium connectors. The same connector is also available in Power Apps, Azure Logic Apps and Copilot Studio.

Microsoft rolls a newly certified connector out to its regions over a couple of weeks. If **Linkly** does not appear in the connector search yet, check again in a few days.

## Connect Linkly to Power Automate

1. In a flow, click **New step** (or the **+** button) and search for **Linkly**.
2. Pick an action, for example **Create or update a link**.
3. Power Automate asks you to create a connection. Click **Sign in with Linkly**.
4. Sign in to your Linkly account, choose the workspace this connection should use, and approve the request.

That is all. The connection is bound to the workspace you chose, so every action in a flow that uses it runs in that workspace. To automate a second workspace, create a second connection and pick it in the action's settings.

## Actions

### ➕ Create or update a link

Creates a short link, or updates an existing one when you supply a **Link ID**. The fields match the [New Link form](https://linklyhq.com/create-tracking-links) in Linkly:

* **Destination URL** is the only field you need to create a link.
* **Name** is the nickname shown in your dashboard, and **Note** is a private note.
* **UTM Source**, **Medium**, **Campaign**, **Content** and **Term** are appended to the destination.
* **Meta Pixel ID**, **Google Analytics 4 Tag ID**, **Google Tag Manager ID** and **TikTok Pixel ID** fire retargeting and analytics tags on the click.
* **Open Graph Title**, **Description** and **Image** set the preview shown when the short link is shared on social media.
* **Block Bots**, **Forward Parameters**, **Cloaking**, **Hide Referrer**, **Head Tags**, **Body Tags** and **Enabled** work as they do in the app.

The action returns the new link, including its **short URL** and **ID**, which you can use in later steps.

### 🔍 Get a link

Fetches one link by its ID, with its destination, short URL and settings.

### 📋 List links

Returns a page of the links in a workspace with their click counts. Supports search and sorting, so a flow can find a link by name before updating it.

### 🗑️ Delete a link

Moves a link to the trash. Its short URL stops redirecting straight away, and the link can be restored from the trash in Linkly if it was deleted by mistake.

### 📈 Get click analytics

Returns click counts over time for a whole workspace or for specific links, optionally filtered by date range, country, browser, platform, referrer or ISP. This is the action to use for scheduled reports.

### 🌍 Get click counts by dimension

Returns clicks grouped by one dimension, ordered by count: country, city, platform, browser, referrer or a UTM parameter, for example "clicks by country this month".

### 🌐 List custom domains

Returns the custom domains configured in a workspace, so a flow can pick a valid **Domain** when creating links.

### 🎯 Report a conversion

Records a conversion such as a purchase, sign-up or custom event. Pass the `linkly_cid` value from your landing page URL as the attribution token and Linkly credits the conversion to the link that was clicked. This action needs [conversion tracking](https://linklyhq.com/support/conversion-tracking) on your workspace.

### 🧾 List conversions

Returns the most recent conversions recorded in the workspace.

### 🗂️ List workspaces

Returns the workspaces available to the connection. Actions that take a **Workspace** field show this list as a dropdown, so you rarely need to call it yourself.

## Flows to build

**Shorten every new row.** Trigger on a new row in an Excel table or SharePoint list that holds campaign URLs. Add **Create or update a link** with the row's URL as the destination and its campaign name as the UTM campaign, then update the row with the short URL the action returns. The sheet fills itself in.

**A weekly click report in Teams.** Use a **Recurrence** trigger, call **Get click analytics** for the past seven days, and post the totals to a Teams channel or send them by email. Add **Get click counts by dimension** for a top-countries table.

**Links for every Dynamics 365 campaign.** When a campaign is created in Dynamics 365 or a row is added in Dataverse, create a tracked link with the campaign's UTM fields and store the short URL on the record, so everyone in sales shares the same tracked link.

**Conversions from your CRM.** Store the `linkly_cid` from your landing page in the lead record. When the deal closes, call **Report a conversion** with that value and the deal amount, and the revenue shows up against the link, ad and partner that produced it.

## Things to know

* **One workspace per connection.** The workspace is chosen when you sign in. Create another connection for another workspace.
* **No click triggers.** The connector has actions only. To start a flow when a link is clicked, create a [Linkly webhook](https://linklyhq.com/support/webhooks) that posts to a flow built on the **When an HTTP request is received** trigger.
* **Rate limits.** Listing links is limited to one request every two seconds per workspace, and **Get click counts by dimension** returns a rate-limit error when the limit is exceeded. Add a short **Delay** step and retry if a flow hits either.
* **Not included:** bulk link creation, click exports and domain management. These are available through the [Linkly API](https://linklyhq.com/support/api).
* **Conversion actions** need conversion tracking to be enabled on the workspace; other workspaces receive an error from those two actions.

The connector mirrors the [Linkly API](https://linklyhq.com/support/api). If you prefer another automation tool, Linkly also has [Zapier](https://linklyhq.com/support/zapier-integration), [Make](https://linklyhq.com/support/make-integration) and [n8n](https://linklyhq.com/support/n8n-integration) integrations.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need a Linkly API key to use the Power Automate connector?

No. The connector uses OAuth. When you create a connection you click **Sign in with Linkly**, sign in, choose a workspace and approve it. There is no key to copy or rotate.

### Which Linkly plan do I need?

Any plan, including the free plan. Reporting and listing conversions also needs conversion tracking enabled on your workspace. On the Microsoft side the connector is classed as Premium, so your Power Automate licence must include premium connectors.

### Is there a trigger for link clicks?

Not in the connector. Create a webhook in Linkly that posts each click to a flow that starts with the **When an HTTP request is received** trigger. That gives you the click's country, platform, browser, referrer and parameters in near real time.

### Which workspace do my actions run in?

Actions with a **Workspace** field show a dropdown of the workspaces available to the connection. Actions without one, such as **Get a link** and **Report a conversion**, use the workspace you chose when you signed in.

# How to Make a QR Code for a Video

Paper cannot play a video, but a **video QR code** gets close: a small square on the card in the box, the instruction sheet or the poster, and the phone everybody already carries plays the video. No app to install, nothing to type.

Any video link works. YouTube and Vimeo are the usual choices, but a TikTok, an Instagram Reel, a Loom recording or a video file on your own website can sit behind the QR code just the same.

## Why make it with Linkly?

Most QR generators encode the video's address directly into the QR code, which means the QR code plays that one video forever. Linkly's QR codes point at a short link instead, so:

* **You can swap the video later.** Re-record the setup guide next year and the QR code already printed on ten thousand boxes plays the new one.
* **Every scan is counted**, so you know how many people watched and roughly where they were.
* **The QR code stays small and clean** enough to carry your logo, because it only has to hold a short link.

**Video: Video to QR Code: Play a Video From a Printed Page** — https://www.youtube.com/embed/NbogsMO326Q

Want a QR code that plays a video? Here's how to make one in Linkly: copy the video link, paste it in, and print the QR code on the box, the card or the manual. It plays on any phone, with no app to install, and you can swap the video later without reprinting anything.

- 0:00 — Paper can't play a video
- 0:18 — Copy the video link
- 0:29 — Make the QR code
- 0:55 — Swap the video later
- 1:09 — Every scan is counted

## How to create a video QR code

1. **Copy the video's link.** — Open the video on YouTube, Vimeo or wherever it lives, click **Share**, and copy the link. On YouTube you can tick **Start at** to make the video begin partway through. This is the only time you will touch the video platform.

2. **Sign in to Linkly and click **Create New Link**.** — [Create a free account](https://l.linklyhq.com/l/4a) if you don't have one yet.

3. **Paste the video link into the **Destination** field.** — Give the link a short ending such as `/setup` or `/how-to`, and a **Nickname** such as "Kettle setup video" that you will recognise next year.

4. **Click **Save**.** — The QR code is drawn as soon as the link exists. There is no second tool and no export step.

5. **Download the QR code.** — Click the QR code to style it, then download a **PNG** for print or an **SVG** if it is going on packaging, and hand that to whoever does your artwork. See [SVG QR codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-svg).

6. **Scan it before it goes to print.** — Point a phone at the QR code on your screen. Some phones open the YouTube app and some open the browser; both play the video without an install.

## Swap the video later

This is the part people miss. Open the link in Linkly, paste the new video's link into **Destination**, and save. The QR code that is already printed starts playing the new video the same afternoon, and nobody needs to know.

That makes a printed QR code safe to commit to: a product insert can outlive three versions of the setup video, a museum label can get a better recording, and a conference poster can point at the talk once it has been uploaded.

## Every scan is counted

Every scan is a click on the short link, so Linkly's [QR code analytics](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-analytics) show how many people watched, when, and roughly where. If nobody is scanning, the QR code is probably in the wrong place on the box. If you put the same video on the packaging and the instruction sheet, give each its own short link and QR code and you will know which one people actually use.

## Where video QR codes get used

* **Packaging inserts and product cards**, for the unboxing or setup video.
* **Instruction manuals**, where a two-minute video beats four pages of diagrams.
* **Posters and flyers** for an event, with the trailer behind the QR code.
* **Business cards**, linking to a short introduction.
* **Menus, labels and museum captions**, for the story behind the thing.

## Tips for video QR codes

* **Tell people what they will get.** "Scan to watch the setup video" next to the QR code gets more scans than a bare square.
* **Unlisted videos work.** A YouTube video set to *unlisted* plays for anyone with the link, so the video does not have to appear on your channel.
* **Keep the video short and phone-shaped.** People are usually standing up when they scan. A vertical video under two minutes is watched to the end far more often.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I use an unlisted or private video?

Unlisted works, because anyone with the link can watch. A private video only plays for accounts you have invited, so it is not suitable for a printed QR code.

### Can Linkly host the video file itself?

No. Linkly can host PDFs, but video files need to live on a video platform or your own website. The QR code then links to them.

### Can I see how many people watched?

You can see how many people scanned the QR code, when and roughly where. Watch time and completion stay in the video platform's own analytics.

### Is it free?

Yes. Every Linkly link comes with a QR code, including on the [free plan](https://linklyhq.com/support/free-plan), and the QR codes do not expire.

## Related QR code guides

- **[Create QR Codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/create-qr-codes)** - the complete guide to dynamic QR codes in Linkly

**Available on:** Free, Starter, Pro, Business, Enterprise plans

---

## How it works

1. You create a **shared album** that guests can add to, in Google Photos, iCloud or Dropbox.
2. You put the album's link behind a **Linkly short link**, which draws the **QR code**.
3. The QR code goes on the table cards, the welcome sign or the order of service.
4. Guests scan and upload. Afterwards you can see when people scanned, and change where the QR code goes.

The short link is what makes this better than a free QR generator: the album link is long and unmemorable, the QR code can be redirected later, and every scan is counted.

**Video: Wedding QR Code for Photos: One Scan, Everyone's Pictures** — https://www.youtube.com/embed/o8E8p3YJaag

Want one QR code that collects everyone's wedding photos? Here's how to make one in Linkly: create a shared album, paste its link in, and print the QR code on your table cards. Guests scan and add their photos straight to the album, and after the day you point the same QR code at the photographer's gallery.

- 0:00 — The photos problem
- 0:24 — Album link in, QR code out
- 0:45 — What guests see
- 0:56 — Swap to the gallery afterwards
- 1:09 — When people scanned

## How to create a wedding photo QR code

1. **Create a shared album guests can add to.** — In **Google Photos**, create an album, open its sharing options, switch on the option that lets other people add photos, and copy the link. **iCloud Shared Albums** and **Dropbox** shared folders work too. Google Photos is the easiest when guests have a mix of iPhones and Android phones.

2. **Sign in to Linkly and click **Create New Link**.** — [Create a free account](https://l.linklyhq.com/l/4a) if you don't have one yet. The free plan covers a wedding comfortably.

3. **Paste the album link into the **Destination** field.** — Give the link an ending you could say across a room, such as `/photos` or `/ellie-and-sam`, and a **Nickname** such as "Wedding album" so you can find it again afterwards.

4. **Click **Save**.** — The QR code is drawn as soon as the link exists. Click it to match its colours to your stationery or add a monogram.

5. **Download the QR code and add it to your stationery.** — Download a **PNG** to drop into your own artwork, or an **SVG** for a stationer or printer. See [SVG QR codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-svg) and [adding a logo to a QR code](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-logo).

6. **Test it with a friend's phone.** — Scan the QR code from your screen with an iPhone and an Android phone, and try adding a photo, before anything goes to print.

## What guests see

Guests scan the QR code and land straight in the album, where they can look through the photos so far and add their own. Most can do it from the browser without installing anything. Depending on the album service, some guests are asked to sign in before they can upload: iCloud shared albums always ask for an Apple account, so if many guests use Android phones, Google Photos or Dropbox is the safer choice. Test with a friend before printing.

Put a short line next to the QR code so people know what it is for: "Scan to add your photos to our album" does the job.

## Where to print it

* **Table cards and place cards**, where guests are sitting down with their phones out.
* **A welcome sign** or the bar, for people arriving.
* **The order of service**, which many guests keep.
* **Invitations**, so early photos from the hen do and the stag do land in the same album.
* **Thank-you cards**, pointing at the finished gallery.

## When people scanned

Because the QR code runs through a short link, you can see when people scanned it in [Linkly's analytics](https://linklyhq.com/support/qr-code-analytics). A spike during the speeches, another at about eleven at night. It is oddly lovely to look at afterwards, and it tells you the cards were in the right place.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do guests need an app to add photos?

Usually not. The album opens in the phone's browser. Some album services ask guests to sign in before they can upload, so test with a couple of phones before you print.

### Can the QR code match our stationery?

Yes. Click the QR code in Linkly to change its colours, style and add a monogram or logo, and download it as an SVG for your stationer.

### Can we see how many guests used it?

Yes. Every scan is a click on the short link, so you can see how many people scanned, and when.

### Does the QR code expire?

No. The QR code keeps working for as long as the link exists, including on the [free plan](https://linklyhq.com/support/free-plan).

### Is it free?

Yes. Every Linkly link comes with a QR code, including on the free plan, which covers a wedding comfortably.

## Related QR code guides

- **[Create QR Codes](https://linklyhq.com/support/create-qr-codes)** - the complete guide to dynamic QR codes in Linkly

**Available on:** Free, Starter, Pro, Business, Enterprise plans

# Conversion Tracking

Click counts tell you a link was popular. They don't tell you it made any money.

Conversion tracking closes that gap. When someone clicks a Linkly link and later buys something, Linkly records the sale against the link that sent them — so you can see revenue per link, not just traffic per link.

![Linkly dashboard chart showing clicks and conversions](https://linklyhq.com/img/conversion-tracking-dashboard-chart.png)

## How it works

When conversion tracking is enabled on a link, Linkly adds a short identifier to the destination URL as it redirects:

```
https://yourstore.com/product?linkly_cid=2ejmw.01KYT5RTSHNMMPWWQ18V570TVG
```

That identifier names the click — not the person. It is remembered on the visitor's own device, and when a purchase happens it is sent back to Linkly so the sale can be matched to the click. If a purchase can't be matched to a link, Linkly discards it: your store is already the record of your sales, and Linkly's job is only to say which link earned them.

## Choosing an integration

There are four ways for a sale to reach Linkly, and a link only needs one. Pick the row that matches where the money changes hands.

| Integration | Best for | Setup |
|-------------|----------|-------|
| **Stripe app** | Stripe Payment Links, and any checkout built on Stripe | Install the app from the Stripe App Marketplace, no code for Payment Links |
| **Calendly** | Booking pages, where a booked meeting is the conversion | Connect Calendly in Linkly, no code |
| **Google Analytics 4** | Any site already sending purchases to GA4 | Add one script tag |
| **API** | Custom checkouts, server-side reporting | One HTTP request per sale |

Stripe and Calendly report over their own webhooks, so there is no script to install and nothing to add to the page. The other two rely on the Linkly script running on your site. When you paste a Stripe Payment Link or a Calendly page into the New Link form, Linkly points you at the right one.

### Stripe

Install **Linkly Conversion Tracking** from the [Stripe App Marketplace](https://marketplace.stripe.com/apps/linkly-conversion-tracking), click **Connect to Linkly** in the app, and choose the workspace the Stripe account belongs to. Then, for any link that points at a Stripe Payment Link, switch on **Conversion tracking** in its Tracking & analytics options. That is the whole setup: Linkly passes the click identifier to Stripe as `client_reference_id`, Stripe hands it back when the payment completes, and the sale is recorded against the link, with subscription renewals credited to the link that first won the customer and refunds subtracted.

If you build your own Checkout Sessions, pass the click identifier yourself as `client_reference_id`, or as `linkly_cid` in the metadata. The app is free and read-only. Full details in the [Stripe guide](https://linklyhq.com/support/stripe-integration).

### Calendly

Connect Calendly from **Integrations** in Linkly, then turn on conversion tracking for links that point at a Calendly booking page. Each booking made through one of those links is recorded as a lead conversion. See the [Calendly guide](https://linklyhq.com/support/calendly-integration).

### Google Analytics 4

If your site already sends purchases to GA4, Linkly can read the same event — no second integration and no changes to your existing tracking.

Add this to every page:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.linklyhq.com/linkly.js" async></script>
```

There is nothing to configure and no key to copy — the attribution identifier already names the link, and a link belongs to one workspace, so Linkly works out where the sale belongs on its own.

Linkly watches for the GA4 `purchase` event and records a conversion when one fires, reading the transaction ID, value and currency from the event you're already sending. It works with gtag.js and with Google Tag Manager.

To track something other than purchases, list the events you want:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.linklyhq.com/linkly.js" data-ga4-events="purchase,generate_lead" async></script>
```

To turn the GA4 bridge off and report conversions yourself, add `data-ga4="false"`.

### Reporting a sale yourself

For a custom checkout, report the sale from your own code:

```js
linkly('track', 'purchase', { amount_cents: 4999, currency: 'USD', event_id: 'order-1234' });
```

Server-side reporting is more reliable and is the better choice where you have the option, because it can't be blocked by the browser. Read the attribution identifier with `linkly('id')`, send it to your backend along with the order, and report the sale from there.

## Making sure it works

Always send an **event ID** — your order number is ideal. Linkly uses it to recognise a sale it has already seen, which is what stops a purchase being counted twice when a customer refreshes the confirmation page.

A few things worth knowing:

- **Only clicks on tracked links count.** Conversion tracking is enabled per link, so turn it on for the links you want measured.
- **A sale is credited to the most recent link the visitor clicked.** If someone clicks two of your links, the later one gets the credit.
- **Attribution isn't instant to set up.** A conversion can only be matched if the visitor arrived through a tracked link after the integration was live, so give it a day or so before judging the numbers.

## Privacy

The identifier Linkly adds to your links is random. It identifies a click, not a person, and it carries no personal information — it can't be traced to an individual by anyone who sees it.

Where an integration sends customer details, Linkly stores them separately from the sale itself, so a deletion request removes the person without destroying the record of which link earned the revenue.

## Troubleshooting

**No conversions are appearing.** Check the link has conversion tracking enabled, then click it yourself and confirm `linkly_cid` appears in the address bar on arrival. If it doesn't, the link isn't tracked. For a Stripe Payment Link, the New Link form and the Traffic page both say whether the Stripe app is connected to this workspace; if it isn't, nothing is recorded until it is.

**GA4 purchases aren't recorded.** Confirm the `purchase` event actually fires by watching GA4's DebugView while placing a test order. Linkly reads the same event, so if GA4 doesn't receive it, neither will Linkly.

**Numbers don't match my store exactly.** They shouldn't. Linkly counts only sales it can trace to one of your links; your store counts every sale. A gap between the two is the point of the feature, not a fault.

# Jotform Integration - Track Which Links Get Forms Submitted

> Connect Jotform to Linkly and see which short links turn into form submissions. Every submission is recorded as a conversion against the link that was clicked.

Source: https://linklyhq.com/support/jotform-integration

# Linkly & Jotform

Click counts tell you a form link was popular. They don't tell you whether anyone filled the form in.

Connect Jotform and Linkly records each submission as a conversion against the short link that was clicked. You can then compare links by submissions, not only by clicks: which email, which ad, which QR code, which social post actually brings in the leads.

## What you need

- A Linkly account. The free plan works.
- A Jotform account. Any plan works; webhooks and API keys are available on all of them.

## Connect Jotform

1. In Jotform, open **Settings**, then **API**, and click **Create New Key**. Set its permissions to **Full Access**. Linkly needs this to add a hidden field and a webhook to the forms you choose.
2. In Linkly, open **Integrations**, choose **Jotform**, paste the key and click **Connect Jotform**.
3. Linkly checks the key with Jotform and shows the account as connected. The key is stored encrypted and is never shown again.

## Choose the forms to track

Your forms are listed under the connected account. Click **Track submissions** next to each form you want to follow.

Tracking a form makes two changes to it, and nothing else:

- A hidden short-text field called **Linkly click id** (unique name `linkly_cid`). Nobody filling in the form sees it.
- A webhook that tells Linkly when the form is submitted.

**Stop tracking** removes the webhook. The hidden field stays, because deleting a field in Jotform deletes its answers from every past submission.

## How it works

When someone clicks a tracked link, Linkly adds a short random identifier for that click to the form's address as it redirects, as `linkly_cid`. Jotform puts it into the hidden field, and when the form is submitted the webhook hands it back to Linkly, which matches the submission to the click.

A few things worth knowing:

- **Only tracked links count.** Submissions that didn't come through a Linkly link with conversion tracking on are ignored. Linkly never sees the rest of your submissions.
- **An edit is not a second submission.** When a respondent edits their submission, the original conversion stands and no new one is added.
- **The identifier names a click, not a person.** It is random and carries no personal information.
- **Jotform hosts the form page.** Because the form lives on jotform.com, there is no page of yours to put the tracking script on, and none is needed.

## Disconnect

Open **Integrations**, choose **Jotform**, and click **Disconnect**. Linkly removes its webhook from every tracked form and deletes the stored API key. Conversions already recorded stay in your reports.

You can also revoke the key from Jotform's API settings at any time; Linkly will then ask you to reconnect.

## Troubleshooting

**"Jotform did not accept that API key."** Check that you copied the whole key, and that it is a Full Access key. A Read Access key can list forms but cannot add the field or the webhook.

**The hidden field is showing on the form.** Occasionally Jotform adds the field without the hidden setting. In the Form Builder, open the field's properties, go to **Advanced**, and switch on **Hide Field**. Linkly shows a note next to the form when this is needed.

**Submissions aren't appearing.** Check that the form is tracked and that conversion tracking is on for the link, then click the short link yourself and confirm the form's address contains `linkly_cid=` followed by a code with a dot in it.

---

# Typeform Integration - Track Which Links Get Forms Filled In

> Connect Typeform to Linkly and see which short links turn into form submissions. Every completed form is recorded as a conversion against the link that was clicked.

Source: https://linklyhq.com/support/typeform-integration

# Linkly & Typeform

Click counts tell you a form link was popular. They don't tell you whether anyone filled the form in.

Connect Typeform and Linkly records each completed form as a conversion against the short link that was clicked. You can then compare links by submissions, not only by clicks: which email, which ad, which QR code, which partner's link actually brings in responses.

## What you need

- A Linkly account. The free plan works.
- A Typeform account. URL parameters are a free Typeform feature. Webhooks, which carry the responses to Linkly, are listed on Typeform's paid plans (Basic and up); if Typeform refuses the webhook when you switch tracking on, that is the reason.

## Connect Typeform

1. In Linkly, open **Integrations** and choose **Typeform**.
2. Click **Connect Typeform** and approve access on Typeform's screen.
3. You are returned to Linkly with the account shown as connected, and a list of its forms.
4. Switch on **Tracking** for each form you share through Linkly links.

Switching tracking on does two things in Typeform: it adds a URL parameter named `linkly_cid` to the form (Typeform calls these hidden fields), and it registers a webhook that sends Linkly each completed response for that form. Nothing else about the form changes.

## How it works

When someone clicks a tracked link, Linkly adds a short random identifier for that click to the form's address as it redirects, as `linkly_cid`. Typeform reads it into the form's `linkly_cid` parameter, sends it back to Linkly with the response, and Linkly matches the submission to the click.

A few things worth knowing:

- **Only tracked links count.** Submissions that didn't come through a Linkly link with conversion tracking on are ignored. Linkly never sees the rest of your responses.
- **Your own URL parameters still work.** If your links already carry `#email=` or `#source=` parameters, they are passed through untouched. `linkly_cid` travels alongside them.
- **Partial responses don't count.** Linkly only records completed forms.
- **The identifier names a click, not a person.** It is random and carries no personal information. The respondent's name and email are attached to the conversion only when your form asks for them.

## Embedded forms

If the short link goes to a page on your own site that embeds a Typeform, rather than to typeform.com directly, the embed has to pass the parameter through. In the embed's advanced options switch on **Read URL parameters**, or add `data-tf-transitive-search-params="linkly_cid"` to the embed code. Alternatively, use [conversion tracking with linkly.js](https://linklyhq.com/support/conversion-tracking) on that page instead.

## Disconnect

Open **Integrations**, choose **Typeform**, and click **Disconnect**. Linkly removes its webhooks from your forms and deletes
